why: The capability marker is only credible if the PRODUCER can be rebuilt. This banks the exact source delta, the base it applies to, and the binary it produced, so the causal claim -- the compiler emitted the value from its own parsed flag -- is checkable rather than asserted.

base.note: The frozen lineage is NEVER modified. G0-G4 verify the effective tree, so instrumenting it in place would invalidate every earlier gate.

built.build_shim: vpython3 -> python3; depot_tools wrapper fails on Python 3.13

delta_2.what: route 2: FlowGraphCompiler records inline_id_to_function -- the inliner's own post-optimization decisions -- and ElfWriter emits them as .note.shorebird.inlining (owner Shorebird, note type 2).
delta_2.bug_found_and_fixed: A ZoneGrowableArray global segfaulted gen_snapshot: it allocates in the current zone, which does not outlive one compilation, so the pointer dangled by the time the ELF writer ran. Malloc-backed storage persists for the process.

route2_witness.encoding: header lines, then records=N, then N records of 12 length-prefixed "<len>:<bytes>" fields: per side library URI, owner, VM kind, declared name, parent kind, parent name. No separators.
route2_witness.note_sha256_covers: the FULL note section bytes as they appear in the ELF (note header + owner + payload), not the stripped payload. An earlier transcript line hashed the stripped payload and so shows a different value for the same artifact; both were equal across the two builds.

replay.semantics: INCREMENTAL, applied in order with patch -p1 from the frozen base. 0001 is a patch against the frozen files; 0002 is a patch against frozen+0001, NOT a cumulative patch. The first version of 0002 was cumulative and therefore ambiguous about which recipe reproduced the binary.
replay.verified: frozen + 0001 + 0002 reproduces the built clone byte for byte across all three files.
